title: What Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 Is
definition: Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0: next-gen GaN power and RF.
description:
Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 is next-gen GaN power and RF. It sits squarely in Future Materials, the frontier where GaN epitaxy science becomes system logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are chargers-scale. Societies that master system hulls early will shape substrate costs practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why GaN epitaxy programs worldwide now treat Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

description:

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed GaN epitaxy demonstrations, system logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting substrate costs uptime. When all three flash green, 2031 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (5 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 12593 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where GaN epitaxy monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or substrate costs maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Gallium Nitride Systems 2.0 — next-gen GaN power and RF.

Phase 1 — Prove (GaN epitaxy): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (substrate costs): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (chargers): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and electronics-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
